KEY MESSAGE 1...The remnants of Hurricane Isaias will impact 
the area Sunday into Sunday night, bringing moderate rain, 
breezy conditions, and a low threat of a tornado.

The primary forecast concern is for Sunday into Sunday night,
when the remnants of Hurricane Isaias in the Gulf will be
impacting our region. Isaias made landfall yesterday evening in
the western Florida panhandle and now continues to interact 
with an upper trough. Extratropical transition is ongoing and
the resultant hybrid low will continue northward into the 
Tennessee Valley through Saturday night, and then northeastward 
in the direction of our area on Sunday.

Guidance has come into good consensus that Isaias's remnants
will impact our region beginning Sunday and into Sunday night, 
and perhaps lingering into early Monday. Widespread moderate to
locally heavy rainfall will be the primary sensible impact,
along with breeze ESE winds during the daytime and into the
evening hours on Sunday. PWats are modeled to be in the 1.5-2+ 
inch range, so while the rain should be mainly stratiform in
nature, some periods of convectively enhanced heavy rainfall 
will be possible, especially later in the day and into the
evening. Rain will push out of the area overnight, but some
showers and drizzle will likely linger overnight and into
Monday.

The rainfall forecast has remained mostly unchanged from 
before, and we expect a widespread 1-2" rainfall event across 
our area, with potentially for isolated amounts up to 3" 
possible. Guidance continues to shift where the heaviest
corridor of rainfall will be, but continues to most likely be
somewhere along the I-95 corridor and southeast, though
confidence on narrowing down the exact location remains very
low. WPC has maintained most of the region in a Marginal Risk 
(1 of 4) Excessive Rainfall Outlook for Sunday, meaning at least
isolated instances of flooding will be possible. Flooding is 
not anticipated to be a significant concern with this event, 
however some localized minor urban and poor drainage flooding is
possible along with ponding on roads. There are currently no 
river gauges forecast to reach flood stage, however if the axis 
of heavier rain shifts north into northern NJ (especially in the
2-3" range), this could cause some gauges in the Raritan basin 
(namely the Millstone River) to rise to near minor flood stage.

ESE winds will increase to 10-20 mph on Sunday, with gusts up 
to 30 mph possible (perhaps up to 40 mph along the immediate
coast). Temperatures will remain steady in the upper 50s and 60s
much of the day. Long story short, a wet and breezy Sunday.

Aside from the rain, with the system lifting over our region, 
shear and CAPE may reach values just high enough to support some
isolated severe storms Sunday evening into Sunday night. Our 
southern zones remain in a Marginal Risk (1 of 5) Severe 
Thunderstorm Outlook for Sunday, mainly for the low risk of a 
brief, weak tornado or damaging wind gust. Some rumbles of 
thunder will be possible by Sunday evening with the rain.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Minor tidal flooding possible with Sunday 
morning's high tide, mainly for coastal areas within Delaware 
Bay. A Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect for Kent County, DE. 

With a period of east/southeasterly flow expected and the 
upcoming New Moon, increased tidal levels are expected later 
this weekend. This will result in spotty to widespread minor  
tidal flooding, mainly for coastal communities along Delaware 
Bay. The only forecast point currently forecast to reach 
widespread minor is Bowers Beach. As a result, went ahead an
issued a Coastal Flood Advisory from 7 AM to 1 PM for Kent
County, DE. 

This won't be a significant event for the Atlantic Ocean coastline,
where only spotty minor tidal flooding is expected from 
Barnegat Bay on south. This includes the Delaware Beaches and 
back bay communities in Sussex County, DE. 

The eastern side of Delaware Bay in NJ and northern part of the
Bay near Reedy Point are also only expected to reach spotty 
minor. Overall though, this event will be nothing like late 
September.

The current forecast has no tidal flooding for areas along the 
Atlantic coastline north of Barnegat Bay. The forecast for the 
tidal Delaware River and Chesapeake Bay also has tide levels 
staying below flood stage at this time.
